summary: Jokai Hiraoka was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1943–1948) and Kyoto University. He later served as a professor at Otemae University (~1966–1989) and worked at Shuchiin University (~1989–1995).

Jon Kabat-Zinn studied at Haverford College and MIT under Salvador E. Luria, also learning from Jack Kornfield, Joseph Goldstein, and others. He founded the Stress Reduction Clinic and served as a professor at the University of Massachusetts Chan Medical School (~1979–2000).

Jonardon Ganeri is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Cambridge, King's College London, and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal. He held posts at Nottingham, Liverpool, Sussex, NYU, and became Bimal K. Matilal Distinguished Professor of Philosophy at Toronto around 2020.

Jonathan A. Silk specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Educated at Oberlin and the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez, he held academic positions at Western Michigan University, Yale University (1998–2002), and the University of California, Los Angeles (~2002–2007).

Jonathan C. Gold works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He has taught at the University of Vermont, served as Assistant Professor of Asian Religions at Drew University (attested 2006), and held faculty posts in religion at Princeton University (attested 2015–2016).

Jonathan Christopher Cleary was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed doctoral studies in East Asian Languages and Civilizations at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi and taught as an instructor at Wesleyan University.

Jonathan Edwards was an American philosopher and religious thinker. He studied at Yale University (~1716–1722), where he later held a post from around 1724 to 1726, before serving at Princeton University in 1758.

Jonathan Geen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his doctorate at McMaster University under Phyllis Granoff by 2001. He has taught at McMaster University, Butler University, and the University of Rochester.

Jonathan Glover is a philosopher educated at Tonbridge School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford. He served as a fellow and tutor at New College, Oxford (~1967–1998), held a post at King's College London (~1998–2013), and was a research fellow at Oxford.

Jonathan Lear was a philosopher who studied at Yale, Cambridge, and Rockefeller University. He taught at Yale (1978–1996), Cambridge and Clare College (1979–1985), and served as John U. Nef Distinguished Service Professor at the University of Chicago (2014–2022).

Jonathan Mark Kenoyer is an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at Woodstock School and the University of California, Berkeley (~1974–1983) and became the George F. Dales Jr. & Barbara A. Dales Professor of Anthropology at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1985).

Jonathan Z. Smith was a religious studies scholar who studied at Haverford College, Yale University, and Yale Divinity School. He held posts at Dartmouth and UC Santa Barbara before serving as Dean of the College at the University of Chicago (1977–1982).

Jong Cheol Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Seoul National University and earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo under Yasunori Ejima. He was a researcher at Mysore (1992) and associate professor at AKS (attested 2001).

Jong-Nam Choi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Shitennoji University and completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg in 1998 under Lambert Schmithausen, also studying with Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, Albrecht Wezler, and David Seyfort Ruegg.

Jongmyung Kim is a Buddhist studies and history scholar. He studied at Yonsei University, Seoul National University, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He served as Associate Professor of Korean Buddhism at the Academy of Korean Studies (attested 2012–2019).

Jos Gommans is a historian and Indologist who studied at Radboud University Nijmegen and Leiden University under Jan Heesterman and André Wink. Since 1993, he has served as associate professor of South Asian history at Leiden University.

Josef Horovitz was a scholar of religious studies, history, and archaeology. He completed his doctoral studies under Eduard Sachau (~1895–1898) and later held an academic post at Goethe University Frankfurt from around 1914 to 1931.

Josef Schick was a linguist who studied at Tübingen, under Albrecht Weber, and completed a PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at Berlin, Bonn, Heidelberg, and served as ordentlicher Professor at the University of Munich (1896–1925).

Josef Strzygowski was an art historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Munich (~1883–1885). He held academic posts at the University of Graz (~1892–1909), the University of Vienna (~1909–1933), and Åbo Akademi University (~1925–1928).

Josef van Ess was a scholar of religious studies who completed his studies at the University of Bonn (~1953–1959). He subsequently held an academic post at the University of Tübingen from around 1969 to 1999.
